findings.passage: "Maybe spending a little bit more time just existing as a human is what I'll be doing," she said.
findings.problem: The article's last sentence is its most perishable claim: a 2026 forward plan (C119, time_sensitive). The closing section is built entirely from one July 2026 promotional encounter (the Vogue cover story timed to Verity). Its first paragraph stacks four facts that do nothing for the type argument and will age fastest: age 36, the June 2025 breakup, wanting children, and promoting Verity. Remove that Vogue piece and the whole ending disappears, even though the body's thesis survives. Nothing here becomes false, because each line is dated or attributed. But the first time she announces a slate, a child or a new relationship, a reader meets an ending about a 2026 crossroads that has already resolved, and a line about slowing down that may read as ironic. The durable insight is the recurring one: wrap grief she has felt "I don't even know how many times."
findings.acceptance_test: The final sentence of the article states or illustrates the recurring pattern (wrap heartbreak, the set as what she protects) rather than a 2026 plan. If the slowing-down quote stays, it appears earlier in the section and is explicitly framed as something she said in 2026. The breakup, children and Verity material is cut to at most one dated clause or removed. Nothing in the last two paragraphs would need editing if she announced three new films, a child or a new relationship next year.

findings.problem: Several narrator sentences present dated statements as present facts, so they will drift silently. They are: "Her home life now" (C105, a 2026 remark, marked stable); "Tender is her favorite word, tattooed on her forearm" (a 2017 Vogue report, C35, stated as a current fact); "Johnson jokes that she and Jennifer Lawrence 'could be the ultimate internet trolls'" (C109, which has no year or source in the prose and drops the source's conditional, "if we, A, had the time and, B, the interest"); and "with Saoirse Ronan in the cast and due in 2027" (a future release stated in the narrator's voice rather than as Vogue's 2026 report; C43 has a trigger, but the wording expires first). A parenthetical that cites a source does not date a present-tense "now" sentence for a reader five years out.
findings.acceptance_test: Each of the four passages carries an absolute year and source inside the sentence. For example: "In 2026 she called her home life 'Just low-key'"; "Vogue reported in 2017 that tender was her favorite word"; "On a 2026 Vogue podcast she joked that she and Lawrence 'could be the ultimate internet trolls if we, A, had the time and, B, the interest'"; "which Vogue said in 2026 was due in 2027." No narrator sentence uses "now" for a state of her life. C105 and C35 are either reworded so they stay true or marked time_sensitive with a review_trigger.

findings.problem: "What is Dakota Johnson's production company?" is a present-tense status FAQ, but its claims (C127, C128) are marked stable with no review_trigger. Partners, ownership and slate change over five years. FAQ answers are lifted verbatim into search snippets and FAQ structured data, so this is the sentence most likely to be served stale without anyone rereading the body. The two-title list ("TeaTime produced Cha Cha Real Smooth and Daddio") will also read as complete when it is not.
findings.acceptance_test: C127 and C128 are marked time_sensitive with a concrete trigger, such as: recheck TeaTime's status, cofounder and slate at each refresh and whenever a TeaTime production is announced or released. The FAQ answer stays true as the slate grows, for example "its early productions included Cha Cha Real Smooth (2022) and Daddio (2024)."

findings.passage: Dakota Johnson most likely fits Enneagram Type 4, the Individualist, at medium confidence.
findings.problem: This is a medium-confidence, contested typing with a live counterphobic Six rival, and the discriminator ("what her safety is for") rests mostly on promotional self-report from 2017, 2022 and 2026. The evidence record never names what future evidence would reopen the call. The discriminator and interpretation claims (C97, C98, C101) are stable with empty triggers, and the only related research task is generic ("find a critical or non-promotional account"). Over five years the likeliest new evidence is non-promotional: a collaborator's account of a TeaTime production that went wrong, a long-form podcast or memoir, or her own account of the 2026 pause. Without named observables, a refresh cannot tell whether new material moves the read toward Six or confirms Four.
findings.acceptance_test: The evidence record names at least two concrete, observable reopen signals, either in research_tasks or as a review_trigger on the discriminator or interpretation claims. Examples: whether she describes a future production conflict as being misled or left unprotected (toward Six) or as the work being made false (Four); whether she credits steadiness to preparation and trusted authority (Six) or to feeling free to feel (Four); and whether she frames the post-2026 pause as seeking security or seeking meaning. It also says when to check: at each refresh, on the release of Three Incestuous Sisters, and whenever a non-promotional long-form account appears.

assessment: Five-year test: the thesis passes. With the whole 2026 Vogue cycle removed (S01, S13, S18 to S22, S33, S34, S42), the Four case still stands on 2017 to 2025 evidence: Fincher's compliment, the Fifty Shades and Madame Web grievances, "I don't have a method," the Lost Daughter remarks about being seen, Foley's 2017 bullshit-meter quote, and the 2017 and 2022 safety-as-precondition lines. The hook also passes. Its contradiction rests on the 2020 and 2021 limes episodes and the 2024 Bustle remarks, and the 2026 Vogue lines are dated. Absolute dates are used almost everywhere. The relative spans check out against the stated dates and the October 4, 1989 birth date: "Ten months later" (March 2020 to January 2021), "five years before" (June 2017 to 2022), "Twelve years later" (2010 to 2022), and "At 36" (for a July 2026 interview). The relationship date matches S01 and S16 (reported June 2025). Changing positions such as the Madame Web reversal and the James non-response are dated and handled honestly. Of the seven non-stable claims, all have workable triggers. The weaknesses are about how the piece ages, not about errors: the ending is a 2026 status snapshot that closes on a plan (future-01); a few present-tense and "now" sentences will drift (future-02); the production-company FAQ has no trigger (future-03); and the contested typing has no named reopen signals (future-04). I raised no major findings. Risk flags: contested_typing (medium confidence, live Six rival) and sensitive_allegations (parents' addiction reporting; the creative-control dispute with E.L. James). Limitations: as the future reviewer I relied on the evidence record's source excerpts and did not reopen URLs. The similarity advisory extracted only two units from this draft, both type-answer sentences, and did not trip (max 0.016 against a 0.04 threshold). Assessed directly, the article is distinctive. The limes, Ellen, Fincher, Easter Bunny and wrap-grief details are specific to her. The "Seven runs from pain" move recurs across the corpus, but here it is tied to her own quote and is ordinary type vocabulary, not reuse.
